transcript.en: We're pleased to welcome Dr. Martin Merry whether of the Antarctic Centre in Christchurch, New Zealand  who has come along to talk to us today about the role of the Centre and the Antarctic Treaty.
transcript.zh: 今天，我们很高兴欢迎来自新西兰基督城，南极中心的马丁·梅里韦瑟博士为我们讲解中心的作用和南极条约。

transcript.en: Now my first question is about the choice of location for the centre.
transcript.zh: 现在，我的第一个问题是关于中心位置的选择。

transcript.en: Why Christchurch?
transcript.zh: 为什么选在基督城

transcript.en: Was it because of the climate?
transcript.zh: 是气候的原因吗？

transcript.en: Well actually New Zealand is the second closest country to Antarctica
transcript.zh: 事实上，新西兰是第二个离南极洲最近的国家。

transcript.en: and Christchurch is often used on Antarctic expeditions.
transcript.zh: 而基督城经常用于南极探险。

transcript.en: Right. So it's because of where we are...coupled with our historical role.
transcript.zh: 好的，所以是因为我们的地理位置和历史作用。

transcript.en: So tell us - what is the main purpose of the centre?
transcript.zh: 那么，告诉我们，中心的主要目的是什么？

transcript.en: Well...we have two complementary roles.
transcript.zh: 我们有两个互补的作用。

transcript.en: One is as a scientific base for expeditions and research and the other is as an information centre.
transcript.zh: 一个是探险研究用的科学基地，另一个是信息中心。

transcript.en: Tell us something about the role as a scientific base.
transcript.zh: 跟我们说说科学基地的作用。

transcript.en: We're able to provide information about what scientists should take with them to the South Pole - for example, the centre contains a clothing warehouse where expeditions are supplied with suitable clothing for the extreme conditions.
transcript.zh: 我们为去南极的科学家提供装备信息。例如，中心包含一个服装仓库，它为探险者在极端条件下提供适当的衣服。

transcript.en: I suppose you need a bit more than your normal winter coat!
transcript.zh: 我猜你要穿得比日常的冬装多一些！

transcript.en: Yes, exactly and then there's also the specialist library and mapping services.
transcript.zh: 没错。还有一个专业图书馆和地图服务。

transcript.en: Right. And which countries are actually located at the centre?
transcript.zh: 好的，中心里面都有哪些国家？

transcript.en: Well...the centre houses research programmes for New Zealand, for The United States as well as for Italy...there is even a US post office at the American airforce base here.
transcript.zh: 中心有新西兰、美国和意大利的研究项目，甚至在美国空军基地还有一个美国邮局在这里。

transcript.en: Really? And what does the visitor's centre offer?
transcript.zh: 真的吗？游客中心是做什么用的？

transcript.en: Well, since very few people will ever experience the Antarctic first hand, the visitors's centre aims to recreate the atmosphere of Antarctica.
transcript.zh: 既然很少有人亲自去过南极洲，那么游客中心的目的在于创造一个南极洲的气氛。

transcript.en: There's a mock camp site where you can see inside an Antarctic tent and imagine yourself sleeping there.
transcript.zh: 里面有一个模拟营地，你可以看到南极洲帐篷里面的样子，并想象自己睡在那里。

transcript.en: And the centre also acts as a showcase for the unique international co-operation which exists in Antarctica today.
transcript.zh: 中心还像是一个展厅，展现如今位于南极洲独特的国际合作。

transcript.en: What is it actually like at the South Pole?
transcript.zh: 南极到底是什么样？

transcript.en: I know you've been there on a number of occasions.
transcript.zh: 我知道你去过那里很多次。

transcript.en: Yes. I have and each time I'm struck by the awesome beauty of the place.
transcript.zh: 是的，每一次我都被那里令人敬畏的美丽打动。

transcript.en: It's magnificent but you can really only visit it in the summer months.
transcript.zh: 很壮丽，但是你只能在夏季去那里。

transcript.en: October to March.
transcript.zh: 十月到三月。

transcript.en: Yes, because it's completely dark for four months of the year...and in addition, it has to be the coldest place on earth.
transcript.zh: 是的，因为一年中有四个月是完全黑暗的，它也是地球上最冷的地方。

transcript.en: Colder than the North Pole?
transcript.zh: 比北极还冷？

transcript.en: Why's that?
transcript.zh: 为什么会这样？

transcript.en: Well, unlike the North Pole, which is actually a frozen sea,  Antarctic is a land mass shaped like a dome, with the result that the winds blow down the slopes at speeds of up to 150km an hour and that's what makes it so cold. And one other interesting things is that Antarctic is the driest continent on earth, surprisingly, and so you have to drink large amounts of water when you're there.
transcript.zh: 它不像北极是冰冻之海，南极像一块圆顶形的陆地，风从斜坡上以每小时150公里的时速吹下，使这里变得极为寒冷。而且另一件有趣的事情是南极洲竟然是地球上最干旱的大洲，所以当你抵达那里后得喝大量的水。

transcript.en: How old is Antarctica?
transcript.zh: 南极洲多大了？

transcript.en: We're pretty sure it was part of a larger land mass but it broke away from the rest of the continent 170 million years ago.
transcript.zh: 我们确认它曾是一块大陆的一部分，但是在1.7亿年前与剩下的大洲断开了。

transcript.en: How can you be certain of this?
transcript.zh: 你怎么能这么确定？

transcript.en: ...because fossils and rocks have been discovered in Antarctica which are the same as those found in places such as Africa and Australia.
transcript.zh: 因为在南极洲发现的化石和岩石与在非洲、澳洲等地发现的一样。

transcript.en: Amazing...to think that it was once attached to Africa.
transcript.zh: 太神奇了，想到它曾经与非洲相连。

transcript.en: Now let's just have a look at the Antarctic Treaty，
transcript.zh: 现在让我们看看南极洲条约。

transcript.en: How far back does the idea of an international treaty go?
transcript.zh: 国际条约的想法可以追溯到多久以前？

transcript.en: Well, as far back as the 19th century, when eleven nations organised an international event.
transcript.zh: 远至19世纪，在11个国家组织一场国际会议的时候。

transcript.en: When was that exactly?
transcript.zh: 具体是什么时候？

transcript.en: And it was called the Polar Research Meeting.
transcript.zh: 它被称作极地研究会议。

transcript.en: And then, not long after that, they organised something called the First International Polar Year.
transcript.zh: 不久之后，他们组织了第一次国际极地年。

transcript.en: And that took place when exactly?
transcript.zh: 具体是什么时候？

transcript.en: Over two years from 1882 to 1883.
But it wasn't until the 1950s that the idea of an international treaty was proposed.
transcript.zh: 但是直到20世纪50年代，国际条约的想法才被人提出。

transcript.en: And in 1959 the Treaty was actually signed.
transcript.zh: 在1959年，条约签订了。

transcript.en: What do you see as the main achievements of the treaty?
transcript.zh: 你觉得条约的主要成就是什么？

transcript.en: Well, firstly it means that the continent is reserved for peaceful use.
transcript.zh: 首先，它意味着大洲用于和平目的。

transcript.en: That's Article One, isn't it?
transcript.zh: 这是第一条，对吗？

transcript.en: Yes...
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.en: That's important since the territory belongs to everyone.
transcript.zh: 这很重要，因为这片领土属于所有人。

transcript.en: Yes but not as important as Article Five, which prohibits any nuclear explosions or waste disposal.
transcript.zh: 是的，但是它没有第五条重要，即禁止任何核爆炸和废物处理。

transcript.en: Which is marvellous. Well, I'm afraid we're going to have to stop there because I'm afraid we've run out of time.
transcript.zh: 太了不起了。恐怕我们今天得到这里了，因为我们没有时间了。

transcript.en: Thanks for coming along today and telling us all about the centre and its work.
transcript.zh: 谢谢你今天的到访，并讲述了中心和它的作用。
